title: Bone Gnawer Democracy
summary: Why the tribe elects its elders.

claims.text: Bone Gnawer tales say that when democracy reached Athens the tribe took it up, choosing elders by vote instead of letting them fight or scheme for rank.
Every member gets an equal say, metis included, which other tribes found hard to accept; the tribe saw it as a way to hold moots without violence.

title: Sept of the Seventh Hill
summary: An early urban caern beneath Rome.

claims.text: Old tales put an ancient caern near where Rome would stand, which made the Seventh Hill sept among the earliest great city caerns.
Defending it taught the Bone Gnawers to guard the Veil and to learn from human politics, and families of the tribe lived in the catacombs below the city.
By Roman times the tribe was strong and organised, helping humans in need and at times fighting the Glass Walkers and Shadow Lords and winning.

title: The Great Pipings
summary: Bone Gnawer tribal moots called across continents.

claims.text: Gatherings called Great Pipings spread through the tribe, and monthly tribal moots became common even though many members never attend.
In the Age of Exploration, a few Bone Gnawers led by the hero Corazon Bitefinder slipped aboard ships to the New World, and a later Piping was held in Lisbon.

title: Bone Gnawer Kin in Other Lines
summary: How the tribe's blood turns up among other Garou.

claims.text: Much of the tribe's Kinfolk comes from groups once treated as outsiders; American Bone Gnawers watched over the waves of European immigrants.

By the late 1800s the tribe had Kin among Irish and Scottish families, and descendants who earned glory were often taken in by the Fianna, so many Garou carry a Bone Gnawer ancestor they would rather hide.
Some wanderers leave children behind on purpose, trusting Rat to provide; tribal Theurges oppose this and ask elders to look after the abandoned Kin.

title: The Hood
summary: A Bone Gnawer camp that robs the greedy to help the poor.

claims.text: The Hood marks greedy and exploitative people, Wyrm-tainted or simply slumlords and crooked officials, and takes from them, then spends the take on getting people out of poverty and addiction.
The camp also shields the homeless and helpless of the cities, which has brought it into growing fights with supernatural predators.

Its charity has hard limits: anyone who abuses the help gets no second chance, and although elders have threatened its members with exile for breaking the law of the Garou, the threat seldom stops them.
